title: Bounded Lipschitz cylinder multipliers and finite Q3 weighted products
question: Can the finite Q3 shifted form domain admit bounded finite-support C1 multipliers with bounded gradient, beyond the Weyl subclass, with explicit same- and cross-orientation weighted products?
method: Take a finite-support multiplication cylinder A_f with sup norm M and gradient norm L, and use the exact kinetic product rule while retaining the nonnegative shifted potential.
Derive q_K[A_f psi] <= 2 M^2 q_K[psi] + L^2/chi ||psi||^2 on either closed EXP-001131 form, giving a same-orientation squared weighted bound 2M^2+L^2/chi.
Use the EXP-001131 degree-six form order to obtain the cross-orientation squared bound 21(2M^2+L^2/chi).

Audit the regularized coordinate a(x)=x/sqrt(1+x^2), whose exact squared modulus and derivative are bounded by one, over rational grids and support sizes, with Lean R304 checking the rational constants.
finding: Primary 46/46, independent 44/44, integrated 15/15, and Lean R304 PASS. The declared bounded finite-support Lipschitz cylinder class preserves both shifted Q3 form domains. Its same-orientation weighted square-root product has squared bound 2M^2+L^2/chi; cross-orientation products pay the exact factor 21. The regularized-coordinate product family satisfies M<=1 and L^2<=m for support size m, uniformly in volume within the degree-six graph class.
decision_reason: The bounded cylinder bridge now extends beyond Weyl multipliers to an explicit finite-support C1 class with a product-rule form estimate. This is the correct bounded QFT test-algebra direction, but it does not license unbounded polynomial observables, modular dynamics, or a common infinite-volume alpha.

fixed-support volume uniformity and independent Lean cross-check
open: all bounded local observables without explicit gradient control

adversarial_review.check: M and L are explicit hypotheses; no coordinate or polynomial with infinite sup norm is admitted.
The form coefficient is exactly 2M^2 with additive L^2/chi from the product rule; no extra factor is hidden in the stated bound.
The EXP-001131 per-site shift makes onsite-plus-bond potential nonnegative, so the potential term is controlled by M^2.
Same and cross products are separated, with cross factor 21 inherited from the closed form comparison.
Only support size and local M,L enter the constants within degree six; no thermodynamic dynamics is inferred.
Unbounded products, modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
